title: MR-JE-AX451 shows "Ab" after weekend power-down
machine: Mitsubishi MELSERVO-JE servo amplifier (MR-JE) with HG servo motor

source_evidence.quote: The display shows "Ab". | A controller, which is not compatible with the servo amplifier, has been connected. | Check if a controller, which is not compatible with the servo amplifier, is connected. | Connect a compatible controller. | [B]
source_evidence.fact: An "Ab" display can be caused by connecting a controller that is not compatible with the servo amplifier, and the action is to connect a compatible controller.

source_evidence.quote: A SSCNET III cable was disconnected. | Check if "Ab" is displayed in the corresponding axis and following axes. | Replace the SSCNET III cable of the corresponding axis.
source_evidence.fact: If a SSCNET III cable is disconnected, "Ab" appears on the affected axis and following axes, and the cable should be replaced.

observations: On Monday 06:40, operator powered up Packaging cell F and MR-JE-AX451 displayed "Ab" immediately; axes AX452 and AX453 also showed "Ab".
The cell had been powered down since Friday 22:00 for a weekend energy-saving shutdown; no hardware changes were recorded.
Maintenance log shows the SSCNET III cable between AX450 and AX451 was last replaced 14 months ago.
A new simple motion module was installed on the line controller three weeks ago but had run without issue until this weekend.

expert_facts.fact: On this line, a weekend cold shutdown often causes the CNIA connector at AX451 to sit 0.5 mm loose; reseat it before replacing any cable.
The 2019 retrofit left a spare compatible controller in the cabinet; swapping to it cleared a similar "Ab" event in 2022.
If reseating CNIA does not clear "Ab" within one power cycle, power-cycle the previous axis AX450 first.
The simple motion module's servo series [Pr.100] was left at default after the March firmware update and must be set to the MR-JE series code.

misconceptions: Replacing the SSCNET III cable immediately is wrong because the manual lists disconnected connectors as a separate, quicker check.
Replacing the MR-JE-AX451 servo amplifier is premature because "Ab" on following axes points to an upstream cause, not a failed amplifier.

title: Intermittent AL. 17.4 Board Error on MR-JE-AX205
machine: Mitsubishi MELSERVO-JE servo amplifier (MR-JE) with HG servo motor

source_evidence.quote: 17.4 | Board error 3 | (1) | The servo amplifier recognition signal was not read properly. | Disconnect the cables except for the power supply, and then check the repeatability.
source_evidence.fact: Alarm 17.4 indicates the servo amplifier recognition signal was not read properly, and the manual recommends disconnecting all cables except power to check repeatability.

source_evidence.quote: It is repeatable. | Replace the servo amplifier. | It is not repeatable. | Check (2).
source_evidence.fact: If the alarm is repeatable after disconnecting cables, the servo amplifier should be replaced; if not repeatable, further checks for environmental causes are needed.

observations: AL. 17.4 occurs intermittently on MR-JE-AX205, about 2–3 times per shift, only when the machining cell A is running at high spindle load.
The alarm resets successfully after power cycling, but reappears within 30 minutes during production.
No other alarms are present; ambient temperature near the cabinet is 42°C, and a new welding machine was installed 5 meters away last week.

expert_facts.fact: Intermittent AL. 17.4 on MR-JE-AX205 often traces to 24V control wiring routed alongside the spindle motor cables in the same duct.
Before replacing the amplifier, I always re-seat the CN1 and CN2 connectors three times to clear oxidation on the pins.
If the alarm is not repeatable with cables disconnected, I check the shield grounding of the encoder cable at the motor end first.
We had a similar case in 2022 on Line 5 where a nearby welding machine caused AL. 17.4; adding a ferrite core on the 24V line fixed it.

misconceptions: The junior suggests immediately replacing the servo amplifier, but the manual says to first disconnect cables and check repeatability; if not repeatable, the amplifier is likely fine.
The junior thinks the alarm is caused by a faulty encoder and wants to replace the motor, but AL. 17.4 is a board error related to recognition signal reading, not encoder failure.

observations: At 08:15 on 2025-06-10, the packaging cell F HMI showed three intermittent communication timeouts to the FX5-PLC616 over the simple CPU communication link.
The simple CPU communication diagnostics buffer showed error code 0x1F2E (communication timeout) at 08:15, 08:22, and 08:29.

A new Ethernet switch was installed in the panel on 2025-06-09 to replace an older unmanaged switch.

expert_facts.fact: On this line, the simple CPU communication retry count was increased from 3 to 5 in March 2024 after similar dropouts during high-traffic periods.
The senior expert always checks the simple CPU communication error code in the special device before touching any cable, because 80% of past intermittent faults were caused by a busy network segment.
A similar intermittent dropout occurred in 2023 when a vision camera was added to the same switch; separating the camera onto a different VLAN resolved it.
When retries are observed, the expert first reviews the communication retry count and time-out period in the simple CPU communication settings before checking physical cables.

misconceptions: The junior suggests immediately replacing the FX5-PLC616 CPU module because the communication status shows 'Communications impossible'.
The junior believes that rewriting the parameters during operation is safe and will not affect communication stability.

title: Intermittent tool sensor dropouts after adding pass-through wiring
machine: OMRON i4L SCARA robot

source_evidence.quote: All USER connector pin associations between the Primary Interface Panel and the Secondary Interface Panel are one-to-one.
source_evidence.fact: The USER connector pins on the Primary and Secondary Interface Panels are directly connected one-to-one.

source_evidence.quote: There are no twisted-pair conductors between the USER connectors on the Primary Interface Panel and the Secondary Interface Panel. Data communication is not recommended for these connectors.
source_evidence.fact: The USER connectors lack twisted-pair conductors, so using them for data communication is not advised.

observations: i4L-R930 at Plant Hanoi, Line 2, Dispensing cell D: tool sensor readings intermittently drop out about 3–5 times per shift.
Dropouts began after a new cable was run through the USER connectors for a tool-mounted RS-232 barcode scanner.
The scanner occasionally reports checksum errors, and the robot's XIO input for the tool sensor flickers.
No robot alarms are triggered; the robot continues motion but dispensing sometimes misses a part.

expert_facts.fact: On this cell, route any tool-side serial data through the XBELTIO RS-232 port instead of the USER pass-through pins.
The site's 24 VDC tool sensor wiring uses a 0.5 mm² twisted pair from the XIO connector, not the USER pass-through.
Past intermittent tool sensor faults on i4L-R930 were traced to induced noise from a nearby servo drive cable bundled with the USER pass-through wiring.

misconceptions: Replacing the tool sensor immediately is wrong because the manual states the USER pass-through pins are one-to-one and not for data, so the dropouts are likely wiring-related.
Adding a ferrite bead to the USER pass-through cable is wrong because the manual warns data communication is not recommended on these connectors.

title: Robot won't move after control power restored, high power not enabled
machine: OMRON i4L SCARA robot

source_evidence.fact: Control Power must be present before High Power can be enabled.

observations: i4L-R957 at Plant Bac Ninh, Line 12, Machining cell D: after a power dip, the robot boots up and shows no alarms, but will not move when the operator presses Start.
The Control Power LED on the robot is on; the High Power LED is off.
The teach pendant shows 'High Power OFF' and the safety gate is closed.
The operator cycled the Control Power switch twice in the last 10 minutes.

expert_facts.fact: On i4L-R957, the High Power enable relay is wired through a safety gate switch that occasionally sticks open after a power dip; tap the gate switch housing to seat it.
The site's XSYSTEM jumper plug for High Power enable is a custom shorting plug that can loosen after thermal cycling; reseat it before replacing any servo amplifier.
A 2021 power dip on Line 12 caused the High Power contactor coil to fail open; check coil resistance (should be ~120 ohms) before ordering a new robot.

misconceptions: Replacing the servo amplifier is wrong because the manual says Control Power must be present before High Power can be enabled, and the High Power LED is off, indicating an enable circuit issue.

Restarting the robot by cycling Control Power repeatedly is wrong because the manual states robot motion is not possible until High Power is supplied and enabled, which requires proper safety circuit continuity.

title: F6.6 cam control inactive after cam data write on MR-JE-AX353

observations: At 06:42 on Monday shift start, MR-JE-AX353 at Plant Binh Duong, Line 5, Pick-and-place cell E showed alarm F6 with detail number F6.6 on the seven-segment display.
The junior operator says cam data for the pick-and-place profile was downloaded from the engineering laptop about ten minutes earlier, and the amplifier was not power-cycled afterward.

If F6.6 persists after a correct power cycle and home return, check parameter PA05 home position offset before replacing any hardware.

title: F0.3 Vibration tough drive warning recurs on pick-and-place cell D
machine: Mitsubishi MELSERVO-JE servo amplifier (MR-JE) with HG servo motor

Check the machine status for screw looseness or others.
source_evidence.fact: The F0.3 vibration tough drive warning occurs when machine resonance repeatedly changes the machine resonance suppression filter setting, and the remedy is to set that filter and inspect the machine for screw looseness.

observations: On MR-JE-AX548 at Plant Hai Phong, Line 2, Pick-and-place cell D, alarm F0.3 appears on the drive display about 3 to 5 times per shift.
The warning started after the X-axis ball screw was re-greased and the coupling was re-tightened during last weekend's PM.

The junior technician pulled the alarm history with MR Configurator2 and saw the resonance suppression filter value differs between morning and afternoon logs.

expert_facts.fact: On cell D, first check the four M4 screws of the X-axis ball screw nut bracket with a torque wrench at 2.5 Nm before touching any filter parameter.

source_evidence.quote: The server function of FTP (File Transfer Protocol) used to transfer files to an external device is supported. An external device equipped with the FTP client functions can handle the files (data logging file, etc.) in the SD memory card installed on a CPU module as follows.
source_evidence.fact: The FX5 CPU module supports an FTP server function that lets an external FTP client access files such as data logging files on the SD memory card.

source_evidence.quote: | Login Name | Set the login name to be used for file transfer request (login) from the external device. | 12 characters maximum (one- byte alphanumeric character) (Default: FXCPU) |
source_evidence.fact: The FTP server login name parameter accepts a maximum of 12 one-byte alphanumeric characters, with a default value of FXCPU.

observations: Since 08:15 today, the line-side FTP client at FX5-PLC646 has failed 7 out of 10 attempts to download the previous shift's data logging CSV from the SD card.
Each failed attempt shows '530 Login incorrect' on the client, then succeeds after the operator re-enters the credentials manually.
The client configuration file was updated yesterday during a Windows patch; the login name field now contains a 14-character string that was auto-generated.
The SD card has 1.2 GB free and the CPU module's FTP server setting is 'Use' with default login name FXCPU.

expert_facts.fact: The auto-generated 14-character login name exceeds the 12-character limit, so truncate it to the first 12 characters and store that value in the client profile.
At Plant Hanoi, the FTP client on Line 1 Inspection cell E has a known bug that appends the domain suffix to the login name after a Windows patch.
Before changing any FTP credentials on FX5-PLC646, always export the current SD card logging files via a direct USB card reader as a backup.
If login still fails after truncation, check the CPU module's FTP server login name parameter first, not the Ethernet cable or switch port.

misconceptions: Replace the SD memory card because intermittent FTP failures usually indicate card wear or corruption.
Reboot the CPU module and the FTP client immediately, since a power cycle will clear any login name length mismatch.

source_evidence.fact: Alarm 8A on the MR-JE is a communication time-out error for USB, serial, or Modbus RTU.

source_evidence.quote: (2) | A communication cable was disconnected. | Replace the communication cable, and then check the repeatability. | It is not repeatable. | Replace the communication cable.
source_evidence.fact: If a communication cable was disconnected, the manual directs replacing the cable and checking repeatability before replacing the servo amplifier.

source_evidence.quote: It was not transmitted. | Transmit a command. | [A] [B] [C]
source_evidence.fact: When no command was transmitted from the personal computer or controller, the corrective action is to transmit a command.

observations: At Plant Da Nang, Line 5, Assembly cell C, MR-JE-AX580 tripped alarm 8A.1 three times during the 06:00 shift startup while the junior was commissioning with a laptop.
The alarm appears only when the laptop is connected by the front USB port; the drive has run all week without alarm when the laptop is disconnected.
The USB cable was recently routed around the cabinet door hinge and shows a sharp bend at the connector.
Pressing the alarm reset on the servo amplifier clears 8A.1, but it returns within 2 to 5 minutes if the cable is moved.

expert_facts.fact: On MR-JE-AX580, first wiggle the USB connector at the drive while watching the alarm; if it trips 8A.1 within 10 seconds, replace the cable before touching the amplifier.
The last three 8A.1 events on Line 5 were caused by a damaged USB cable at the cabinet door hinge, not by the servo amplifier.
Keep the laptop USB cable strain-relieved with a 50 mm service loop so the MR-JE front connector is not loaded when the door closes.
Before replacing MR-JE-AX580, confirm the laptop terminal software is actively sending commands, because an idle USB session can also trigger 8A.1.

misconceptions: The junior wants to replace MR-JE-AX580 immediately because alarm 8A.1 is present, but the manual requires checking whether a command was transmitted and replacing the communication cable before replacing the servo amplifier.
The junior believes alarm 8A.1 means the servo amplifier is internally faulty, but the manual lists no command transmission and a disconnected communication cable as earlier causes to check.

title: FX5-PLC866 serial link drops with 7F68H framing error after VFD install
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote:
• The stop bit settings do not match.
• A disturbance occurred in the line due to power supply ON/OFF of the target station.
• There is noise on the line.
• At the time of multi drop connection, the data is sent simultaneously from multiple devices.
source_evidence.fact: A framing error (7F68H) is caused by mismatched stop bit settings, line disturbance from power cycling of the target station, noise on the line, or simultaneous transmission from multiple devices in multi drop connection.

source_evidence.quote:
• Reduce the communication speed and then execute communication again.
• Check if momentary power failure has occurred on the station with the CPU module (using the special register SD1005).
source_evidence.fact: For an overrun error (7F67H), the manual advises reducing communication speed and checking special register SD1005 for momentary power failure at the CPU module station.

observations: FX5-PLC866 at Plant Dong Nai, Line 9, Assembly cell E reports error code 7F68H on its RS-485 serial channel to the barcode scanner about 8 to 12 times per shift.
The faults started on Monday morning, two days after a new VFD was installed on the same panel to drive the cell's conveyor.
Each fault clears after a power cycle of the PLC, but returns within 20 to 40 minutes of running.
The scanner is daisy-chained on a multi drop link with a second scanner and a weigh scale on the same two-wire bus.

expert_facts.fact: On this cell, 90 percent of framing errors trace back to the scanner's 9600 bps / 8-N-1 setting being changed to 8-E-1 during a firmware update.
The new VFD on panel 9 was wired with its motor cable in the same tray as the RS-485 bus, which injects noise; a 30 cm separation and a ferrite on the bus cleared a similar 7F68H event in March 2023.
Before touching any parameter, the senior expert always checks SD1005 for momentary power failure at the PLC station, since a 20 ms brownout on the 24 V rail mimics a framing error.
The site workaround is to drop the bus from 19200 bps to 9600 bps and enable the scanner's 50 ms inter-character timeout until the VFD cable is re-routed.

misconceptions: Replace the FX5-PLC866 CPU module immediately, because the 7F68H code is assumed to mean the PLC serial port is damaged.
Re-terminate the RS-485 shield at both ends of the bus to 'improve grounding', which actually creates a ground loop and worsens the noise-induced framing errors.

title: Intermittent NAK 7F69H parity errors on FX5-PLC919 inspection cell link
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote: 7F69H | Parity error | • The parity bit settings do not match. • A disturbance occurred in the line due to power supply ON/ OFF of the target station. • There is noise on the line. • At the time of multi drop connection, the data is sent simultaneously from multiple equipments. | • Match the settings of FX5 programmable controller and counterpart equipment. • Take counter measures for noise. • At the time of multi drop connection, have an interlock so that the data is not sent simultaneously from multiple devices.
source_evidence.fact: Error 7F69H is a parity error caused by mismatched parity bit settings, line disturbance from target station power cycling, line noise, or simultaneous multi-drop transmissions, and is resolved by matching parity settings, adding noise countermeasures, or interlocking multi-drop sends.

source_evidence.quote: When two or more errors occur at the same time, priority is given to the error code with the smallest number, and the error code with the smallest number is sent. Further, in case of an occurrence of the following errors, initialize the entire transmission sequence.
source_evidence.fact: When multiple errors occur simultaneously, the smallest-numbered error code is reported, and for these errors the entire transmission sequence must be initialized.

observations: FX5-PLC919 at Plant Hanoi, Line 2, Inspection cell B reports NAK error code 7F69H roughly 3–5 times per 8-hour shift.
Errors cluster within ±10 minutes of the 06:00 and 14:00 shift changes when the vision camera and barcode reader cabinets are powered on.
The PLC and the two counterpart devices are on an RS-485 multi-drop link; all three currently use 9600 bps, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, even parity.
No cable or connector changes were made in the last 30 days, and the errors disappear when the camera cabinet is left powered.

expert_facts.fact: On this cell, 90% of 7F69H bursts trace to the vision camera cabinet sharing the same 24 VDC supply as the barcode reader, so check that supply first.
Before touching parity settings, scope the RS-485 A/B pair for ringing above 1.5 V at the PLC end during camera boot.
Since 2022, the site has added a 120 ohm termination resistor at the far end and a ferrite on the camera cable to suppress these shift-change 7F69H alarms.
For multi-drop interlock, site practice is to delay camera and reader power-up by 5 seconds after the PLC reaches RUN, using the PLC's Y10 output.

misconceptions: Replacing the FX5-PLC919 CPU module immediately, because the error is logged in the PLC, ignores that 7F69H is a line-level parity fault usually caused by noise or simultaneous multi-drop transmission, not a CPU failure.
Changing the parity bit setting on the PLC from even to none without matching the camera and reader will not fix the issue and will itself create the parity mismatch described in the manual.

title: FX5-PLC298 MC Protocol Error 7E41H During Random Read
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote: | 7E41H | Data length error | The number of points that can be exchanged at the time of random reading/writing are exceeded and specified. | Check the sent message of the counterpart equipment, modify it if necessary, and then execute communication again. |
source_evidence.fact: Error 7E41H indicates a data length error with too many points specified for random reading/writing, requiring the sent message to be checked and modified.

observations: At 08:15 on Line 12, Machining cell F, the SCADA system logged error code 7E41H from FX5-PLC298 during a random read request.
The error occurred three times in 10 minutes after a new recipe was downloaded to the line controller at 08:05.
The random read request was for 300 points from D registers starting at D5000.
No changes were made to the PLC program or wiring; only the recipe parameters were updated.

expert_facts.fact: The FX5 PLC allows a maximum of 192 points per random read command, so requests must be split into chunks of 192 or fewer.
The line controller's default random read block size is 256 points, which exceeds the FX5 limit and must be manually adjusted to 192.
In 2022, a similar error occurred after a firmware update that reset the block size to 256; the fix was to set it to 192 in the controller's communication settings.
Always verify the random read point count in the SCADA message log before assuming a hardware fault.

misconceptions: Replacing the FX5 PLC communication module because the error suggests a hardware fault.
Increasing the timeout value for the random read command, as the error is caused by too many points, not slow response.

title: FX5-PLC963 RD LED Off, SD LED On – No Data Reception on Line 12
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote: Off | On | Data is being transmitted but not being received.
source_evidence.fact: When the RD LED is off and the SD LED is on, the module is transmitting data but not receiving any.

source_evidence.quote: If the LEDs are not flashing, check the wiring and the communication settings or the master station or other local station setting.
source_evidence.fact: If the LEDs are not flashing, the wiring and communication settings of the master or local station should be checked.

observations: At 14:20 on Line 12, Assembly cell D, the junior noticed the RD LED on the FX5-PLC963 communication module is completely off while the SD LED is solid on.
The PLC is still sending data to the master station, but no data is being received; the HMI shows stale values from 14:18.
No recent changes to the PLC program or wiring were reported, but a new cable was installed last week between the PLC and the network switch.

expert_facts.fact: On FX5-PLC963 at Line 12, a solid SD with RD off usually means the receive pair is reversed; first swap the orange and white-orange wires in the RJ45 plug.
The site had a similar incident in March 2024 when a replacement cable used stranded wire instead of solid core, causing intermittent receive failure after two weeks.
Always verify the master station's send LED is flashing before touching the PLC end; if the master is silent, the fault is upstream.
The local parameter for the FX5-PLC963 receive timeout is set to 100 ms; if the master polls slower than that, RD may appear off even with valid data.

misconceptions: The junior might immediately replace the communication module, but the manual states that if LEDs are not flashing, wiring and settings should be checked first.
A less experienced person might assume the master station is faulty and reset it, but the expert knows that reversed receive pair or incorrect cable type is a more common cause on this line.

title: FX5-PLC388 SLMP error C05BH during inspection cell B data read
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote: C05BH Ethernet module cannot read or write data from/to specified device. Reconsider device to read or write.
source_evidence.fact: Error C05BH occurs when the Ethernet module cannot read or write the specified device, and the remedy is to reconsider the device to read or write.

source_evidence.quote: C05CH Error in request contents. (Reading or writing by bit unit for word device, etc.) Correct request content, and send to Ethernet module again. (Subcommand correction, etc.)
source_evidence.fact: Error C05CH indicates a request content error such as reading or writing by bit unit for a word device, and the fix is to correct the request content and resend.

observations: At 14:20 on Line 5, Inspection cell B, the SCADA HMI showed SLMP error code C05BH while trying to read D100 from the FX5-PLC388.
The error appeared three times in 10 minutes only when the operator requested a 32-bit counter value from D100.
A recent change was made to the SCADA recipe: the tag for D100 was changed from word to bit access at 13:50 today.
The PLC communication LED is green and other tags on the same Ethernet connection update normally.

expert_facts.fact: On FX5-PLC388, D100 is used by the line's reject counter and is overwritten every 50 ms, so reading it as a bit causes C05BH.
Check the SCADA tag's data type first; 9 out of 10 C05BH calls on this cell were wrong device type, not hardware.
If the tag must stay bit, move the counter to M100 and read that bit instead of D100.
After correcting the tag, clear the error history in the Ethernet module diagnostics before retesting.

misconceptions: Replace the FX5-ENET/IP module because the error suggests a hardware failure.
Power-cycle the PLC to clear the error without checking the SCADA tag configuration.

title: N:N Network link error on FX5-PLC476 at Pick-and-place cell D
machine: Mitsubishi MELSEC iQ-F FX5 PLC communication network

source_evidence.quote: When a link error occurs in the master station or local station of the N:N Network, the data transfer sequence error flag turns ON.
source_evidence.fact: A link error in any N:N Network station causes the data transfer sequence error flag to turn ON.

source_evidence.quote: When the data transfer sequence error turns ON, the error code is stored in the following device.
source_evidence.fact: The error code is stored in a specific device when the data transfer sequence error turns ON.

source_evidence.quote: Serial communication errors are not cleared even after communication has recovered its normal status.
source_evidence.fact: Serial communication errors remain latched even after communication returns to normal.

observations: At 09:15, the FX5-PLC476 master station at Plant Da Nang, Line 2, Pick-and-place cell D showed SM9040 ON (data transfer sequence error flag for station 0).
Error code SD9061 contained 0x0A (hex), indicating a data transfer sequence error on the master station.
The junior reported that the error appeared after a brief power dip on the 24V DC supply to the N:N Network segment; communication seemed normal afterward but the error flag stayed ON.
The line was stopped for 12 minutes while the junior tried to clear the error by cycling power to the PLC, but the error flag remained ON after restart.

expert_facts.fact: On this cell, a power dip often leaves the N:N Network error latched; clear it by turning ON SM50 for one scan, not by cycling power.
Historical data shows 80% of N:N link errors here trace to a loose shield on the drop cable to station 3, not to the PLC itself.
Always check the terminating resistor DIP switch on the last station (station 7) before replacing any communication module.
The site uses a 100 ms debounce on the N:N error input to avoid nuisance trips from contactor noise on the same panel.

misconceptions: Replacing the FX5 PLC communication module immediately is wrong because the manual states errors are not cleared by power cycling and the root cause is often cabling or termination.

Turning OFF and ON the power to clear the error is wrong because the manual says devices are cleared only by power OFF→ON, STOP→RUN, reset, or SM50 ON, and a simple power cycle may not clear the latched error if the sequence is not followed.

title: Intermittent Modbus RTU time-out on packaging cell A

source_evidence.quote: 8E.8 | Modbus RTU communication CRC error | SD |
